pass_a_gloss: What need is there for the silence of others and often and especially now, and to me, both willingly and unwillingly, being forced to be silent and being compelled to silence. For I have neglected thus the good and fine words, which are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain unimpeded sequence. For I have not been able to accomplish this charming Greek work. But now eight years have passed for me, since which I have not been able to write or say anything great or small, nor have I heard anyone else writing or saying anything, except for the wonderful men who have established the beautiful philosophy, for whom elegance and simplicity of names are of less concern. But placing their voices second, they wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision. I do not think they are unwilling, but rather very willing to pour out the good and precise thoughts in speech. But perhaps they are not able, since they have the sacred and God-given and divine word in the words, which is difficult for each person to grasp, and to encompass the human soul, which is complex and human. If indeed silence is a friend and helper to the mind and discovery, the eloquent is not found anywhere else, but in voices and continuous practice. But the mind is also seized by another kind of learning, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I wanted to say something, even small, to the Greek voice, our wonderful men, who now direct the affairs of all humans under the same authority, being precise and varied and wonderful, and being called most Greek, expressed and handed down in the Roman voice, which is persuasive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. Since, however, our words are like images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters, and with technique, and with the material of colors, not only similar, but also varied and beautiful, to write out the writings with the many-mixed of flowers, without hindering, we would agree.

pass_b_english: Why is there need for the silence of others, and often, and especially now, and for me, both willingly and unwillingly, being forced into silence and compelled to keep quiet? For I have neglected thus the good and fine words, which are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain unimpeded sequence. (John 1:1) For I have not been able to accomplish this charming Greek work. But now eight years have passed for me, since which I have neither myself said or written anything great or small at all, nor have I heard anyone else writing or speaking privately, or even delivering public panegyric and competitive speeches, except for those wonderful men who have established the beautiful philosophy, for whom elegance and simplicity of names are of less concern. But placing their voices second, they wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision. I do not think they are unwilling, but rather very willing to pour out the good and precise thoughts in speech. But perhaps they are not able, since they have the sacred and God-given and divine word in the words, which is difficult for each person to grasp, and to encompass the human soul, which is complex and human. If indeed silence is a friend and helper to the mind and discovery, the eloquent is not found anywhere else, but in voices and continuous practice. But the mind is also seized by another kind of learning, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I wanted to say something, even small, in the Greek voice. Our wonderful men, who now direct the affairs of all humans under the same authority, being precise and varied and wonderful, and summed up as 'most Greek,' expressed and handed down in the Roman voice, which is persuasive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. Since, however, our words are like images of the passions of our soul, to those who are able to speak, like good painters, and with technique, and with the material of colors, not only similar, but also varied and beautiful, to write out the writings with the many-mixed of flowers, without hindering, we would agree. (Psalm 19:1)
